title: Rewind of one loop head
statement: Let $c,C,q$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $h$ assign integer positions to the $c+1$ work heads, let $o$ be an output word, and choose a head index $i<c+1$. For any natural number $j\le q$, starting in rewind state $i$ with head $i$ at position $j-1$ and the other heads at their positions in $h$, after exactly $j+1$ steps the machine is in advance state $i+1$, with head $i$ at position $0$, the other heads unchanged, and output still $o$.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns integer positions to all work heads
replaced:
From the rewind state of loop level $i$ with head $i$ at displacement $j-1$,
for any $j \le q$, exactly $j+1$ steps reset head $i$ to displacement $0$ and
enter the advance state of level $i+1$; the other loop heads and the
accumulated output are unchanged.
